heading: Against a published AF chip
sub: MIT-BIH Atrial Fibrillation database, 128-interval segments, held-out subjects, all choices made inside the folds. Published chip: Andersson et al. 2015 (figures tuned on the data they report).

rows.title: Accuracy
rows.verdict: Matches (not a win: the intervals are about 8 points wide)

rows.title: Size

lines.text: 831 gate-equivalents at synthesis, 55 flip-flops included; about 1,440 at layout.
About 29 times fewer at synthesis, about 17 times at layout.

rows.caveat: The published chip does more (an ectopic-beat filter, entropy, a 1,664-bit memory) and uses a different cell library, so this is not the same function made smaller.

lines.text: Specificity 287 of 384, 74.7% (published 79.0%) on the 200-series and 343 of 359, 95.5% (published 97.0%) on the 100-series.
The gate netlist and the model agree on every real interval of both databases (1,221,534 and 109,446), 0 mismatches; the core is formally proved; a proof for every possible input is not closed.

footer: Data: MIT-BIH Atrial Fibrillation Database and MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, PhysioNet, Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0. Method and code: experiments/baselines/af on branch amg/base-af.
